header: Here I ask the AI which utility a line means, for the line that intent.ts cannot settle (a whole sentence in which the plain words of no utility are found). What leaves the plant: the one typed line, with long digit runs and e-mail addresses blanked, and the list of utilities (the app's own text). NOTHING ELSE: not a figure entered in a utility, not a search result, not a person; and never an ID query (maskForAi gives null for it). What comes back is only a utility's id (or "none") and a confidence: I check the answer against the real list of utilities, so a made-up id, or a sentence, is no answer. The AI never supplies a number or a fact: the utility itself, once opened, does that from its own source.

symbols.name: parseAiAnswer
symbols.sig: export function parseAiAnswer(text: string): AiPick | null
doc: The AI's reply, checked: a real utility id and a confidence between 0 and 1; null for "none", for an id that is not in the list, or for anything that is not that JSON.

symbols.name: askWhichUtility
symbols.sig: export async function askWhichUtility(line: string, generate: (prompt: string) => Promise<string>): Promise<AiPick | null>
doc: Asks `generate` (the AI) and returns its checked pick; null when the line may not be sent, the AI says none, or it fails, and the caller then does what it always did.

symbols.name: AI_MIN_CONFIDENCE
doc: I act on a pick from this confidence up.
